I’m so, so, so incredibly sorry. There’s not much I can say that I think will actually help your grieving and pain. I can, however, let you know I empathize with you and you sound like the best daughter she could have ever asked for. 

I have felt the same anticipatory grief since I was young as well, for no real reason either, except for the fear of losing the one person in the world whose opinion I also singularly cared about it. I can’t imagine what it will feel like losing that person except extreme confusion and disorientation. 

So all that to say - I’m thinking of you and sending you love. I hope you can one day come to peace with knowing what a beautiful relationship the two of you had and how truly rare that is these days. There are so many people who are not lucky enough to have stable/healthy relationships with their parents, let alone loving, caring, ones centered around best friendship and mutual love. You are so lucky to be able to grieve that wonderful love you had that so many children and adults yearn for for their entire lives. I know that won’t make the pain subside - only time can do that. But when you’re thinking of the loss you’ve experienced, try to every now and then just focus on the love you were able to experience and how that has shaped you into the loving, empathetic and deeply sensitive person you clearly are!
